passage: Researchers surveyed adults in four countries about how often they read printed books for pleasure. A journalist summarizing the results claimed that the share of frequent readers was not simply higher in countries with higher incomes.
stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the journalist's claim?
choices: Country C had a lower median income than Country B but a higher share of frequent readers.
Country A had both the highest median income and the highest share of frequent readers.
Country D had the lowest median income and the lowest share of frequent readers.
More than a quarter of adults in every country surveyed were frequent readers.
steps: The claim: reading frequency does not simply rise with income.
Support needs a case where a lower-income country has more frequent readers.
Choices about A and D fit the income pattern, so they work against the claim; the last choice ignores income entirely.
key: To support “not simply X,” look for a counterexample in the data.
source: SAT AIS original item, written to the College Board Digital SAT content specifications
